DE-9IM relations of polygons to the cells their boundaries touch

Source: R/cb_relate.R
cb_relate.Rd

A burn says how much of each cell a polygon covers. The DE-9IM matrix says how the polygon and a cell (a closed box) meet: interiors, boundaries and exteriors, each against each. For almost every cell the burn already answers that: a cell the polygon's boundary does not reach is either wholly inside it (a run) or wholly outside (no record). cb_relate() computes the matrix for the remaining cells, those whose closed box the boundary touches, and stores them in a sixth table, relations. That includes cells the polygon only touches along a wall or at a corner, which have no record in a burn at all.

Usage

cb_relate(x, geom)

Arguments

x

A cb_burn object that has not been cropped.

geom

The geometries that were burned into x, in the same coordinates and order: anything wk::as_wkb() understands. There must be n_geom of them. The burn does not keep its geometry, so it is passed again; passing different geometry gives meaningless matrices.

Value

x, with a relations table. Use cb_burn(relate = TRUE) to get the same from the geometry in one step.

Details

The matrix is read from the geometry, not from the burn's records. The burn treats a coverage within 1e-6 of 0 or 1 as exactly 0 or 1, so a cell holding a sliver of a polygon has no record and a cell holding a sliver of its exterior is a run; the relations see both.

The relations table

One row for each polygon and in-grid cell whose closed box the polygon's boundary meets, sorted by id, row and col:

row, col, id

as in the other tables: 1-based, row 1 at the top, id the position of the geometry plus id_offset.

matrix

the DE-9IM matrix of the polygon against the cell as nine characters, row-major over the polygon's interior, boundary and exterior (rows) against the cell's (columns), each F or the dimension 0, 1 or 2 of the intersection, for example "212F11FF2".

Every other cell of a polygon is "212FF1FF2" if it is in one of that polygon's runs and "FF2FF1212" otherwise, so the runs and the relations together give the matrix of every cell. Lines, points and empty geometries have no relations.

Assumptions

Polygons are assumed valid (rings that do not cross, holes inside their shell, parts of a multipolygon meeting only at points); the matrices of invalid polygons are not defined. Contacts are decided with exact predicates on the coordinates as given, with no snapping, so a polygon offset from a cell wall by 1e-14 does not touch it. For a burn from cb_burn_index() the geometry is moved into index space exactly as it was burned, and the matrix is exact for the rotated or sheared cell; on grids burned in index space by other front ends it is the index-space matrix.

Examples

library(wk)
g <- wkt("POLYGON ((1 1, 3 1, 3 3, 1 3, 1 1))")
b <- cb_relate(cb_burn(g, extent = c(0, 4, 0, 4), dimension = c(4, 4)), g)
b$relations
#>    row col id    matrix
#> 1    1   1  1 FF2F01212
#> 2    1   2  1 FF2F11212
#> 3    1   3  1 FF2F11212
#> 4    1   4  1 FF2F01212
#> 5    2   1  1 FF2F11212
#> 6    2   2  1 212F11FF2
#> 7    2   3  1 212F11FF2
#> 8    2   4  1 FF2F11212
#> 9    3   1  1 FF2F11212
#> 10   3   2  1 212F11FF2
#> 11   3   3  1 212F11FF2
#> 12   3   4  1 FF2F11212
#> 13   4   1  1 FF2F01212
#> 14   4   2  1 FF2F11212
#> 15   4   3  1 FF2F11212
#> 16   4   4  1 FF2F01212
table(b$relations$matrix)
#> 
#> 212F11FF2 FF2F01212 FF2F11212 
#>         4         4         8
